candidates.buyer: Small urban taxi, tricycle and rental operators, interurban travel agencies, own-account goods hauliers

candidates.existing: None seen. No competitor search was run because the search budget was used up.
candidates.name: Road-transport licence and authorisation compliance tracker for small taxi, minibus, tricycle and travel-agency operators (S5 to S10)
candidates.trigger: Prime Minister's decree of 10 Oct 2022 on access to road-transport professions, plus a ministerial note creating licence categories S5 to S10. An authorisation to practise is also needed for each category, and S10 is valid one year and renewable. Compliance deadline was 10 Oct 2023. Licences are individual and non-transferable (a 2019 case suspended a licence for 12 months).
candidates.unchecked: Number of licence holders, renewal cycle for S5 to S9, whether MINT has a state portal for renewals, fleet-management competitors, and willingness to pay among small operators. The competitor search in French was not run.

candidates.buyer: Moto-taxi syndicates and association federations (for example the Douala body Grasmota) and their members
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators
candidates.name: Association-level compliance pack for moto-taxi syndicates and members (carte grise, insurance, inspection, municipal vignette, impôt libératoire)
candidates.trigger: Moto-taxis must hold a carte grise, valid insurance, technical inspection certificate, annual municipal vignette and impôt libératoire. Douala prefect census drive in 2016. Grasmota obtained cartes grises for 1,500 riders in June 2023.
candidates.unchecked: Fee amounts today, whether syndicates collect dues digitally already, and mobile-money use. Riders are low-income, so willingness to pay is likely low.

candidates.buyer: About 200 temporary-work and placement firms approved by the employment ministry, and user companies that must check their approval
candidates.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
candidates.existing: None seen. No competitor search run.
candidates.name: Annual approval, user-company checks and worker-statistics file for ETT and private placement agencies
candidates.trigger: Approval is held for a fixed term with its own expiry date, and a list is published each year. The ministry has asked firms to show approval, statistics of placed workers and made-available contracts. Using an unapproved ETT exposes user firms to fines or suspension.
candidates.unchecked: Legal basis (decree or order number) of the statistics duty, filing frequency and portal, and current agency count. The fetched page did not confirm any reporting deadline. Its relation to K07 and K10 is payroll only, so this is a different buyer and duty. Competitor search not run.

candidates.buyer: Driving-school operators (about 540 dossiers audited) and their union
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
candidates.existing: A state online exam-registration platform run by a contractor (Pressprint, 2018). It handles registration, not school compliance. No private school-management software seen.
candidates.name: Driving-school approval dossier and candidate-registration manager
candidates.trigger: MINT approval needs an opening authorisation, qualified instructors per licence category and compliant documents. Training hours were raised in 2017 to 20 practical and 40 theory hours. Candidates register online for exams, with a fee paid through mobile money. In 2020 an audit found irregularities in 396 of 540 dossiers and gave two months to comply.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the exam registration is still online, current number of schools, whether approval has periodic renewal, and the state of the sector in 2025-26. Dated evidence (2017-2020). Competitor search not run.

candidates.buyer: Private nursery and early-childhood operators
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
candidates.name: Opening-authorisation file tracker for private nurseries, crèches and maternelles
candidates.trigger: Private schools need authorisation of creation, opening and operation. In 2018 about 200 schools, mostly private lay, were closed for lacking them.
candidates.unchecked: The crèche-specific rule (which ministry), annual reporting, and number of operators. The only evidence is a one-off authorisation duty, not recurring.

candidates.buyer: Small waste collectors, scrap and plastics recyclers, businesses that generate waste
candidates.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
candidates.existing: The state BND platform itself, if it goes ahead.
candidates.name: Waste traceability manifest and BND registration helper for waste collectors and recyclers
candidates.trigger: Decree 2012/2809/PM of 26 Sept 2012 covers collection, transport and treatment. The MINEPDED launched the Bourse Nationale des Déchets and a traceability manifest by a letter of 12 Feb 2026. The Prime Minister's secretariat asked for it to be withdrawn pending consultation, and employers' group GECAM objects.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the manifest becomes mandatory, who must file, the legal text, and whether the state BND would replace any private tool. The rule is contested, so this is a watch item.

candidates.buyer: Agro-input shops and professional spray applicators
candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.name: Pesticide retail and applicator compliance file (homologated-product check and applicator approval)
candidates.trigger: Law 2003/003 and decree 2005/077: only homologated or provisionally authorised products may be sold, and professional applicators must be approved. The agriculture minister in 2024 said unregistered, counterfeit and banned products flood markets. The MINADER list of homologated products seen was dated Nov 2015.
candidates.unchecked: Whether retailers must keep a sales register or report to MINADER, shop count, and enforcement frequency. No recurring filing was found.

candidates.buyer: Cattle and small-ruminant traders, transporters, butchers' unions

candidates.trigger: Decree 86/711 of 14 June 1986 requires a livestock passport and sanitary laissez-passer for movements. Inter-region movements need a MINEPIA regional delegate's signature (pig movement rules 2021).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the decree is still the working rule, volumes, and whether any digital movement system exists.

candidates.buyer: Private vets (an old count of 38 installed practices) and veterinary pharmacies

candidates.trigger: Law 90/033 (profession, Ordre membership), law 78/21 and law 2000/018 (veterinary pharmacy, import and installation authorisation).
candidates.unchecked: Current number of practices, any periodic reporting to MINEPIA or the Ordre. The market is very small.

candidates.trigger: Decree 2024/00176 of 26 Feb 2024 sets how water used for agriculture and upkeep of hydraulic works in irrigated perimeters is managed.
candidates.unchecked: The decree text was not opened. Which bodies must collect fees or file reports, how many perimeters exist, and whether users are small businesses. Only the search summary was seen.

coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K06; not searched again per contract.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No licensing text found. A national autonomous union of ferrailleurs exists; Cameroon Tribune (May 2026) says scrap volumes are falling because of foreign industrial buyers. A MINEPDED Bourse Nationale des Déchets (BND) covers metals but its legal basis is still disputed. No register duty found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No pawnbroker or second-hand dealer register found. Only the general commerce law 90/031 (trader card). Nothing found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05; not searched again.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No specific dismantler regime found. Parts dealers are only under general commerce rules, with periodic tax raids (old Afrik.com article).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Decree 86/711 of 1986 requires a livestock passport and sanitary laissez-passer for movements. Movements between regions need a MINEPIA regional delegate's signature (pig case, EcoMatin). Paper-based and handled by state delegates. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No butcher card or register text found. A June 2025 case of 95 cattle slaughtered illegally in Olembé shows enforcement is ad hoc. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper register or export certification found. Production was 4,672 t in 2024, down 50% from 2022. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Law 90/033 (profession), law 78/21 (Ordre) and law 2000/018 (veterinary pharmacy) apply. Very few private practices: an old study counted 38 installed vets. No public register or software found. Weak.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water law 98/005. Decree 2024/00176 of 26 Feb 2024 covers water management in irrigated perimeters. No driller licensing text or abstraction permit found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Decree 2012/2809/PM governs waste collection and transport, with a MINEPDED environmental permit. In 2026 the BND platform and a traceability manifest were launched by a MINEPDED letter of 12 Feb 2026, but the Prime Minister's office asked for it to be withdrawn pending consultation. Rules are in flux.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Cameroon-specific text found; results were all French, Belgian or Polynesian. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: The state plans 300 rural mini water networks (financing round of 4 Mar 2025, FCFA 276bn need). Community management committees exist. No operator register or regulator reporting found. Unverified, future.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Law 2003/003 and decree 2005/077: only homologated products may be sold, and professional applicators must be approved. The minister in 2024 complained of counterfeit and unregistered products. No dealer register or software found. Fertiliser has no dealer regime found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: About 200 ETT and private placement offices hold approval from the employment ministry, and a list is published each year. Firms must show approval, worker statistics and made-available contracts (older Cameroon Tribune article). One candidate logged.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No Cameroonian funeral or cemetery text found. A 2017 press piece shows about 15 funeral firms in Bertoua. Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies
coverage.found: Law 90/053 of 1990 sets declaration for associations and authorisation for foreign and religious bodies. NGO status under a 1999 law needs three years of activity reports. No periodic filing or deadline found. Weak.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Decree of 10 Oct 2022 on access to road-transport professions plus new licence categories S5 to S10 (urban transport up to 11 seats, own-account goods, tricycles, rental, platform taxis). Compliance deadline 10 Oct 2023. Moto-taxis need carte grise, insurance, technical inspection and municipal vignette. Two candidates logged.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers are K04. Street vendors pay the impôt libératoire (turnover under FCFA 10m, paid quarterly) and a communal droit de place. Yaoundé banned wheelbarrow vending in some districts from 20 Jan 2025. No digital register found. Weak.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
coverage.found: Driving schools: 2020 audit found irregularities in 396 of 540 dossiers, and candidates register online. Private schools: about 200 closed in 2018 for lacking creation, opening or operating authorisation. Hunting outfitters: only an old 1998 order found. Two candidates logged.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Placement offices and temp-work firms need a MINEFOP agrément. About 200 hold a valid one. 87 were suspended in 2019, and 178 new operators were approved for 2023. MINEFOP checks approval, placed-worker statistics and contrats de mise à disposition. Guarding firms fall under law 97/021 as amended by 2014/027. Nothing new beyond K10 for security. One candidate on placement/temp-work agencies.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: New Mining Code (law 2023/14 of 19 Dec 2023). Decrees of 19 Nov 2024 on quarries (4 categories; artisanal quarries need a 2-year communal authorisation for Cameroonian individuals) and on title-holder obligations. The 2025 subcontracting law reserves work for local SMEs (51% national ownership). No source found for a register or reporting duty on construction sites. Candidates: subcontracting law, artisanal quarries.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: New CEMAC AML/CFT regulation: awareness seminars on 28-29 Aug 2025 in Yaoundé and Douala, including for designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs). Cameroon is on the FATF grey list. Notaries and real estate agents must file suspicion reports with ANIF. Details of the new regulation not seen. No local compliance software found. One candidate.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: The tourist tax (taxe de séjour) of 1,000-5,000 FCFA per night dates from the 2017 finance law. Hoteliers complain they cannot pass it on and about the classified-establishment regime. Only 2017 sources found; no current register or guest-card rule seen. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02/K03/K08 for timber and cocoa/coffee. Fish: EU imports of Cameroonian fishery products have been suspended since 2009, and relaunch is planned around 2032 under FISH4ACP. Artisanal fish-processing sites are category A. Export health certificate rules for small operators not found.

coverage.category: 31. Private schools and training centres (authorisation, closure campaigns)
coverage.found: MINESEC closed 154 private establishments in July 2025 and 105 on 20 July 2026 (Littoral 52, Sud-Ouest 11, Nord-Ouest 5). MINEDUB suspended processing of private primary school approval requests for 3 months (letter of 10 Aug 2026). A DGI circular of March 2026 clarifies the patente regime for private schools and health facilities. One candidate.

coverage.category: 32. Personal data protection (law 2024/017)
coverage.found: Law 2024/017 of 23 Dec 2024. The 18-month grace period ended 23 June 2026, so the law now applies. It sets consent, minimisation, security and cross-border transfer duties, with fines up to 1 billion FCFA for legal entities. An independent authority, the APDP, is created. Whether the APDP is operational, the processing-register or declaration rules and the decrees are unverified. One candidate.

coverage.category: 33. Gaming and betting (sports betting shops, lotteries)
coverage.found: Gaming law 2015/012 of 16 July 2015 and decree 2019/2300/PM. Online betting licensed (sources point to MINAT; the licensing body is unclear). Minimum age 21. Nothing found on shop-level duties or LONACAM agents. Weak and unverified.

coverage.category: 34. Mobile money agents, payment institutions and sub-agents
coverage.found: Mobile money is about 5% of GDP (GSMA 2025). BEAC decision 013/GR/2022 covers the USSD aggregation platform. A 0.2% tax on transfers and withdrawals dates from 2022. No 2025 rule found on agent approval. Agent KYC/AML register duty not confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 35. Classified establishments (dangerous, unhealthy or nuisance activities) and environmental impact
coverage.found: Law 98/015 of 14 July 1998: class 1 needs authorisation, class 2 needs a prior declaration. Hotel owners' union SPIHT has asked for hotels to be removed from the list. Nomenclature, fee schedule and any 2024-2026 update not found. Weak and unverified.

coverage.category: 36. Subcontracting law 2025 (local-content subcontracting regime)
coverage.found: Bill filed 25 June 2025; per Lextenso, in force since mid-July 2025. 69 articles, 12 sectors, 6 contract types, local SMEs with 51% national ownership first, 30% start-up advance. Authority, registration duty and decrees not confirmed (Lextenso page returned 403). One candidate, shared with category 27.

result.competitor: I found no Cameroon or CEMAC-specific AML compliance software or service for notaries or estate agents; searches in French returned only bank compliance job ads. Foreign tools (Konforme, Legapass, France, per the claim) are not built for CEMAC law. I could not confirm whether ANIF has an online reporting portal (goAML); not found. Bank-focused KYC and screening vendors exist but were not checked for CEMAC DNFBP coverage.
result.duty: CEMAC AML/CFT regulation of Dec 2024 (search results give No. 02/24/CEMAC/UMAC/CM of 20 Dec 2024, 186 articles, replacing the 11 Apr 2016 regulation; I did not read the official text). It applies directly in Cameroon. DNFBPs (notaries, lawyers, bailiffs, real estate agents including letting agents, dealers taking cash of 5M FCFA or more, car dealers, hotels, travel agencies, accountants and others; 22 categories) must check customers, keep records and report suspicions to ANIF straight away. Secrecy cannot be used to refuse ANIF; tipping off the client is forbidden. The 2016 text had cash caps of 5M FCFA (commercial) and 3M FCFA (property); I could not check these in the new text. Supervision goes to each profession's ministry or professional body. MINFI ran outreach seminars in Yaoundé and Douala in Aug 2025. Penalties: the 2016 regime had administrative, disciplinary and criminal sanctions; I did not find the amounts in the 2024 text. Frequency: event-driven, with ongoing customer checks; I found no periodic filing deadline. The FATF Oct 2025 and June 2026 statements keep Cameroon under increased monitoring, all action-plan deadlines have expired, and supervision of DNFBPs is a named action item.
result.market: Small. I found no official count of notaries in Cameroon: a 2017 decree ended the appointments of 24 notaries, and a new decree on the profession's status was signed in 2025. Licensed real estate agents are on a MINHDU register that is being cleaned up; 28 firms were suspended in Aug 2026, mostly in Yaoundé and Douala. Much of the market goes through informal 'démarcheurs'. Other DNFBP categories (car dealers, hotels, travel agencies) are numerous but rarely in AML scope in practice. Realistic paying buyers: probably a few hundred offices (estimate, not verified).
result.reason: The duty is real. A revised CEMAC AML/CFT regulation, reported as No. 02/24/CEMAC/UMAC/CM of 20 Dec 2024, applies directly in Cameroon. It covers more than 20 DNFBP categories, including notaries and real estate agents, and requires customer checks and suspicion reports to ANIF. Under the 2016 text, cash was barred above 3M FCFA in property deals; that threshold is unverified in the new text. Supervision goes to each profession's ministry or professional body. Cameroon is still on the FATF grey list (June 2026), and DNFBP supervision is a named weak point; ANIF said inspections would start soon. I found no CEMAC-specific tool. The weaknesses: there is no fixed recurring filing (suspicion reports are event-driven), enforcement is just starting, buyers are few (notaries number perhaps a few hundred, unverified) and much of the property market is informal. Willingness to pay is doubtful.

The duty is real. Decree 2022/8801/PM of 10 Oct 2022 sets access conditions for road-transport professions. A ministerial note created the S licences, and a separate authorisation to practise is issued centrally. S8 and S10 licences are issued by the central transport directorate. The S10 fee is 15,000 F and the authorisation fee 200,000 F. The compliance deadline was 10 Oct 2022 plus one year. A 12-month moratorium then ran from 10 Oct 2023, so it has expired. S6 issuance was suspended. I found no state renewal portal and no compliance software (two searches only). Weaknesses are that renewal cycles for S5 to S9 and the number of licence holders are unverified, informal operators are unlikely to pay, and licences are issued in person. Willingness to pay is low and the MVP is hard to defend.

Duty is real but thin. MINEFOP publishes yearly lists of approved ETT and placement offices (166 authorised for 2025: 138 ETT and 38 offices, out of about 250 known). It has sanctioned firms for not filing placement statistics, lacking made-available contracts and not renewing approval (87 suspended in 2019; 45-day and 3-month notices). I found no decree number, filing frequency or portal, and no dedicated software. But the market is tiny (about 170 to 250 firms), the user-company check is a one-off lookup in a free published list, and willingness to pay is likely low. The 2023 and 2025 sources are press reports, not the legal text.

Duty is partly supported: 2017 hours rules and 2020 audit come from the claim's own sources, which I did not open. A third-party guide says MINT digitised licence applications on 2 Dec 2024 via ssdtmint.cm, including exam booking and auto-school approval. That makes the state portal the core registration tool. I found no Cameroonian driving-school software, only French products (Klaxo, E-manager), so competition is thin. I found no official text on periodic renewal, no current school count (about 540 dossiers in 2020), and no 2025-26 sector data. Buyers are few, pay little, and depend on a state portal, so the MVP has a narrow scope and weak willingness to pay.

Press and a legal journal say a subcontracting law has been in force since mid-July 2025. It reserves subcontracting to SMEs with 51% national capital and an HQ in Cameroon. It covers 12 sectors, and a subcontracting authority certifies when a foreign firm is allowed. I found no promulgated law number, no Journal officiel text, no implementing decree and no authority name. I found no registry, declaration or platform duty. The only digital tool found is the general eRegistrations platform, which is not specific to subcontracting. Penalties, frequency and the number of firms are unknown. Without a recurring filing duty, this looks like a contract-template or advisory niche. The buyers are fragmented, and the 69-article text comes from the bill, so the final law may differ. Score stays low.
